content: The author, a disabled person in their early 30s, describes feeling unusually “lucky” just to leave the house because everyday activities like going to work, meeting friends, or even seeing people regularly can no longer be assumed. Citing new research from the disability charity Scope, they report that nearly half of working-age disabled people—around 3 million in Britain—say they often or always feel chronically lonely, pointing to an especially severe loneliness crisis among disabled people.***
